# Polynomial acquisition of the exact cover inventory (separate compiler addendum)

**Candidate; independent review pending.** The frozen eleven-file cover theorem
is preserved byte-identically under `frozen_cover_source/`. This addendum removes
its exponential subset enumeration; it does not change its CTMC class, function,
profile constants, inequalities, or stationary conclusions. No new graph-algorithm
novelty is claimed. The derivation is self-contained; no external source is used.
In particular the parent's inaccessible Citeseer maximum-clique source is not
retried, mirrored, read or cited as verified.

## 1. Exact finite circuit, acquired from the graph

Let G be the nonempty satellite graph satisfying the frozen theorem's condition:
no induced triangle plus isolate and no induced P4 plus isolate. For every vertex
v form its anti-neighborhood U_v=V\(N(v) union {v}). The induced graph on U_v contains
no triangle or P4, because v would be the isolated vertex in the forbidden pattern.

Every connected triangle-free and P4-free graph with at least one edge is complete
bipartite. Here is an elementary proof. A shortest odd cycle in a nonbipartite
triangle-free graph has length at least five and is chordless; its first four
vertices form an induced P4. Thus the graph is bipartite. If a connected bipartite
graph omits a cross-shore edge, a shortest path between those two vertices has odd
length at least three, and its first four vertices induce a P4. Contradiction.
Singleton components are isolated vertices. Ordinary BFS two-coloring plus all
cross-pair checks therefore acquires each U_v's biclique components and isolates.
No decomposition is supplied as input.

For arbitrary nonnegative satellite weights x, maximum independent-set weight is

    alpha_x(G)=max_v [x_v + sum_(isolates w in U_v) x_w
                    + sum_(bicliques L,R in U_v) max(x(L),x(R))]. (1)

An independent set containing v consists of v and an independent set in U_v.
On a complete bipartite component it chooses one whole shore; nonnegative weights
permit inclusion of all isolates. Conversely every set on the right is independent.
Every nonempty independent set has an anchor v. An optimum can be taken nonempty
even when every weight is zero. This proves both directions of (1), including ties.

Since complements of vertex covers are independent sets,

    tau(x)=sum_v x_v-alpha_x(G).

# Dyadic gluing across a free-port extinction boundary

**Author-verified ordinary proof candidate; independent review pending.** This is
separate from the finite-layer lemma and every previously accepted archive. The
implementation and exact component checks are retained, but no independent
acceptance, general-WR, or historical-novelty conclusion is being claimed.

## Target raw class

One open species A has0<->A. Internal channels are the reversible binary hub/2A/arm
architecture. There is a satellite F absent from every hub, with EXACTLY ONE arm
A+F<->H0, where H0=B+C. Remove F from the hub graph; the remaining graph satisfies
the accepted dominating-cover condition. All its satellites have arms, every hub
has amplification, and all rates are arbitrary positive. F is acquired by trying
the finitely many isolated satellites and checking its unique arm/core graph; no
good F or hub is supplied as an oracle.

Notation: M=sum of all rare (non-A, non-F) counts, U=A+M, N=F+U. Let d be the number
of rare species, E>=1 the core hub count, a the sum of 2A->hub rates, k_- and k_+
the minimum/maximum forward arm totals on rare satellites, k_F the sole forward
F-arm rate and ell_F its reverse rate. Let b_-=min hub->2A rates, s_+=max total
reverse hub rates, b0=min_h(s_h+b_h), S=sum internal constants, and
F_all=2a+max(k_+,k_F). The core weighted-cover inventory is R=A+tau_Grare.
The protected capture-pair inventory is P=A+min(B,C). Always P<=R<=U.

The constructed global function is

    W=t^N [h0 + eta phi Z],
    h0=g0_R+rho0 A/(R+1)^2-e A/(N+1),
    Z=gF_P-1+rhoF A/(P+1)^2 >=0.

The two profiles are acquired finite backward heads with rational tails. A dyadic
logarithmic cutoff phi is compiled below. It is not a stationary fiber law.

## A. Common one-dimensional profile constructor

For a specified beta>0 and requested t>1 define L=lambda(t-1),

    eps=min(1,(lambda+beta)/2), c=4(L+eps)/beta,
    K=max(2,ceil(2c)),
    g_r=1+c/r for r>=K,
    g_r=(lambda*t+beta*r^2)/(lambda+beta*r^2-eps)*g_(r+1)
       backwards for r=K-1,...,1; g_0=2t g_1.

Let d_r=g_r-g_(r+1)>0. The accepted elementary recurrence proof gives

    lambda(tg_(r+1)-g_r)-beta r^2 d_r <= -eps g_r, r>=1.

Acquire the following finite constants, with displayed tail bounds:

    dlow=min(c,min_(1<=r<K)(r+1)^2 d_r),
    Gratio=max(3,max_(1<=r<=K)d_(r-1)/d_r),
    D1=max(4c,max_(1<=r<=K)(r+1)^2 d_(r-1)),

This is a separate proof draft, not part of the frozen single-free-port theorem.
It uses no new external source or stationary fiber law. No recurrence claim has
received independent review. The earlier target-cover exclusion remains correct
for that resource but need not be an obstruction for this different construction.

## 1. Raw class and the retained core

Start with the binary hub/active architecture of the frozen free-port theorem:
0<->A; every square-free A-free hub H has 2A<->H; every other internal pair is
A+X<->H; each satellite has at least one arm; all rates are strictly positive.
Acquire a nonempty set of isolated hub-graph species F_i, remove their actual
arms and coordinates, and require the residual raw core to pass the admitted
dominating-cover graph test. A sufficient finder takes ALL isolated hub-graph
vertices, so it is not handed a favorable grouping. The remaining graph need
not be complete multipartite or a disjoint union of bicliques. Every F_i may
capture into arbitrary hubs; the union of targets may contain triangles/P4s.

Let F=sum_i F_i, M=total residual rare count, U=A+M, N=F+U. Let

    R=A+tau_core,       J=2A+M=U+A.

Thus U<=J<=2U and R<=U. Every free capture A+F_i->H, and its reverse, preserves
J EXACTLY. Every hub amplification H->2A raises J by2; every reverse rare arm
H->A+X raises J by1. Their forward counterparts lower J by2 or1. Immigration
raises J by2; actual A death lowers J by2. This linear resource counts inactive
rare bulk, so Q need not control J^2. That failure is handled by the core's
low-R/U cone, not denied or supplied as an activation oracle.

Use k=min_i sum_H k_(i,H)>0. Then actual free capture intensity is at least kAF.

rate ratios; no equilibrium of the free composition is assumed.
